title: The Tortoise Who Called Himself All of You
text:
In an Igbo tale, known to many readers from Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart, the birds were invited to a great feast in the sky. It was a time of famine, and Tortoise, whose stomach was always his first thought, begged to come along. The birds did not trust him, but he spoke so sweetly that each bird gave him a feather, and with them he made a pair of wings.

On the way he told them that people invited to such a feast should take new names for the occasion. Each bird chose one. Tortoise chose "All of You."

When the feast was laid out, Tortoise asked their hosts for whom it had been prepared. "For all of you," they answered. "You see," said Tortoise to the birds, "the feast is for me." He ate the best of everything, and the birds got only the scraps. Furious, each bird took back its feather, leaving Tortoise stranded in the sky.

He begged Parrot to tell his wife to bring out all the soft things in the house so he could jump down safely. Parrot told her instead to bring out the hard things: hoes, machetes, spears and pots. Tortoise jumped, fell and crashed down so hard that his shell broke into pieces. A medicine man glued it back together, and that is why a tortoise's shell is not smooth.
lesson: Using the people who help you for your own gain may work once, but it leaves you alone when you need them most.
source: Igbo folk tradition; retold in Chinua Achebe, Things Fall Apart (1958), Chapter 11
